checks.scope: Only a toy data relation. Does not establish K&H's full variation conditions, physical realizability, an organizational closure mechanism or a phenomenal identity.

checks.claim: §12.6.3 CF.1: closure-preserving maps necessarily induce refinement of threat/support partitions
checks.test: Two explicit partitions plus SMT missing-bridge countermodel
checks.result: the alleged implication needs a distinct monotonicity/compatibility axiom
checks.scope: Illustrative formalization, not a physical counterexample to all possible closure morphisms. A stronger definition may restore a functor but must be justified and tested.

checks.result: measure-zero assertion is not universal without an ensemble/measure and a proof of genericity
checks.scope: Countermodel to unrestricted measure claim, not evidence that physical closure networks usually share profiles under a specified continuous distribution.

cases.claim_under_test: S1 Remark 7.4: any finite or countable union of static FNNs has bounded approximation capacity
cases.construction: Countable family of finite static rational-weight ReLU nets f_n(x)=x/n+(2/n)Σ_k ReLU(x-k/n), n positive integer
cases.proof: Each f_n is exact piecewise-linear interpolant; f_n(x)-x²=(x-a)(b-x) on [a,b], length=1/n, hence sup error=1/(4n²)→0.
cases.result: A countable family of individually fixed FNNs approximates a target g not equal to any family member arbitrarily closely; refutes blanket countable-family inference, not Theorem 7.2's fixed-f positive distance.
cases.scope: One explicit target suffices against an unqualified no-arbitrary-approximation claim. Full C([0,1]) density also follows via standard piecewise-linear interpolation but is not machine-proved here.

cases.claim_under_test: S1 Theorem 3.2 labels growing input-history domains a plasticity condition
cases.fixed_weight_model: h_t = h_(t-1) + x_t, y_t = h_t, h_0=0, x_t∈{0,1}; parameters never update
cases.result: The theorem's growing-history-domain premise holds for a fixed-weight recurrent model; its non-equivalence under strict domain matching is not specific to plasticity.
cases.scope: A counterexample to the characterization of the premise as plasticity, not a counterexample to Theorem 3.2 under its stated domain-equality definition.
